materials.title: A 7-day practice plan
materials.body: Day 1: fingerspell your name. Day 2: greetings. Day 3: numbers 1 to 10. Day 4: family words. Day 5: food and water. Day 6: ask three questions using eyebrows. Day 7: hold a one-minute conversation with someone and ask for feedback.

materials.title: Questions and negation in ISL
materials.body: A question is shown with raised eyebrows and a slight head tilt forward. Negation is shown with a headshake, often at the end of the sentence. If your face stays still, the sentence reads as a plain statement.

materials.title: Being a good communication partner
materials.body: Get attention with a wave or a gentle tap on the shoulder. Look at the person, not at the interpreter or the screen. Keep your face visible and well lit. Write or type when a sign is not understood, and never pretend to understand.

materials.title: Fingerspelling without stress
materials.body: Fingerspell at a steady rhythm instead of racing. Read whole words by their shape and rhythm, not letter by letter. Practise with place names and your own surname.

materials.title: Signs you will need at a counter
materials.body: Appointment, form, ticket, platform, account, sign here, wait, repeat, thank you. Learn these nine and a counter conversation becomes much easier.
